data.content_ref: inline:The target's own defense is self-undermining: its mechanism justifies the 'rational choice' to prefer well-corroborated theories by appealing to their 'greatest leverage for further discovery' — an explicitly forward-looking instrumental claim. To warrant acting on a theory because of its expected future leverage, the target must assume that past survival under severe tests is informative about future utility. That assumption is exactly the uniformity-of-nature / future-resembles-past premise that the target's own countercondition 2 identifies as the signature of smuggled induction. The target declares this countercondition but its mechanism's justification triggers its antecedent. The verbal distinction between 'rational choice' and 'inductive inference' collapses because the only substance offered for why the choice is rational is an instrumental projection from past testing history to future payoff. This is distinct from the already-raised Tichý–Miller objection: even if verisimilitude were formally coherent, the defense would still fail because its forward-looking justification reinstates the very inductive commitment Popper rejects.
